description: Literature priors for the L2 vocabulary (docs/plans/l2_knowledge_base_retrieval.md section 5). Every entry cites a source that was looked up, says how it was verified, and compares against this corpus where a comparison is meaningful. Plan D5: when a prior and the corpus disagree, the corpus wins for this tracker and the disagreement is recorded here. Priors are never read by encode or exact decode.
corpus: runs/talkvid-train207__20260923T200526Z__24ffdd5, L2 vocabulary 0.2.0 (talking heads, 206 speakers, 3180 described s)

entries.claim: Spontaneous blink rate depends on the task: mean 17 blinks/min at rest, 26 during conversation, 4.5 while reading (150 healthy adults, video); conversation > rest in 67.3% of subjects.

source.authors: Bentivoglio AR, Bressman SB, Cassetta E, Carretta D, Tonali P, Albanese A
source.title: Analysis of blink rate patterns in normal subjects

entries.claim: Reported spontaneous blink durations differ widely between studies because 'duration' is defined differently (closing phase only vs. full closure-reopening, search coil vs. video). Example: 77.6 +/- 10.0 ms for spontaneous blinks in one magnetic search-coil study, 17.6% shorter than voluntary blinks.

source.authors: Baker RS, Abou-Jaoude ES, Napier SM
source.title: Kinematic Comparison of Spontaneously Generated Blinks and Voluntary Blinks in Normal Adult Subjects

entries.verified: abstract via web search, 2026-09-26; which phase the 77.6 ms covers was NOT confirmed from the full text

corpus_check.value: median 0.23 s (p10 0.13, p90 0.43), measured as the L1 span above rest + 0.1 at 30 Hz
corpus_check.status: not comparable: different definition and a 33 ms grid; do not use as a gate

entries.claim: A felt (Duchenne) smile combines AU12 (zygomatic major, lip corner puller) with AU6 (orbicularis oculi, cheek raiser); AU12 alone is the non-Duchenne smile.

source.authors: Ekman P, Davidson RJ, Friesen WV
source.title: The Duchenne smile: emotional expression and brain physiology. II
source.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

entries.verified: title and AU6+12 definition via web search, 2026-09-26

corpus_check.value: cheekSquintLeft/Right never leave 'none' on this corpus
corpus_check.status: conflict with the tracker, corpus wins (D5): smile has AU12 members only; AU6 cannot be observed through MediaPipe's cheekSquint here

entries.claim: Conversational nods split into fast nods (vertical head movement > 1.5 Hz, mainly while listening / receiving information, a likely backchannel) and slower coordinated nods (< 1.5 Hz).

source.title: Head Nodding and Hand Coordination Across Dyads in Different Conversational Contexts

entries.verified: abstract-level summary via web search, 2026-09-26; preprint, not peer reviewed

corpus_check.value: head_move median 1.07 s (p10 0.40); one L2 head_move is one excursion, not one oscillation cycle
corpus_check.status: not directly comparable; relevant when head_move gains a repeats/frequency parameter

entries.claim: Head movement is more frequent while speaking than while listening; nods are part of the listener's backchannel repertoire.

source.authors: Hadar U, Steiner TJ, Rose FC
source.title: Head movement during listening turns in conversation

entries.verified: existence and summary via web search, 2026-09-26; full text not read

corpus_check.value: TalkVid clips are mostly the speaker's turn
corpus_check.status: expect many head_move per minute (corpus median 24.8); a listening-turn corpus would show fewer
